questions.title: Configuration, not a model nickname
questions.prompt: Only the chat template and decoding settings changed. What is the evaluated object?
questions.explanation: The full versioned system configuration. The weight file is unchanged, but the response distribution is not.

questions.title: Hierarchical resampling
questions.prompt: There are twenty generations for each of twelve prompts. What is the first resampling level for a claim about new prompts?
questions.explanation: Resample prompts as whole clusters. Generations can be resampled within a selected prompt or aggregated by a predeclared prompt-level protocol.

questions.title: Exact McNemar reasoning
questions.prompt: `A_only=9`, `B_only=2`; the asymptotic result crosses 0.05 but the exact value is 0.06543. What is the primary conclusion?
questions.explanation: With only eleven discordant tasks, use the exact binomial result: the evidence does not cross the 0.05 threshold.

questions.title: Coverage and selector quality
questions.prompt: A correct candidate exists in the pool but the selector returns another candidate. Which two booleans describe the run?
questions.explanation: `coverage=True` and `selection_success=False`. pass@k alone does not describe delivered quality.

questions.title: Containment versus Jaccard
questions.prompt: Why can a Jaccard threshold of 0.7 not be copied to benchmark-side containment?
questions.explanation: The denominators differ, so the same text pair receives different values. A detector threshold belongs to its exact metric and calibration protocol.

questions.title: Adaptive test reuse
questions.prompt: A team selects the best of eighty prompts on one private set. Why is that set no longer an independent final test?
questions.explanation: Its feedback selected the configuration, making it part of development. A fresh holdout or a controlled adaptive-query procedure is required.

questions.title: Identity and position
questions.prompt: A judge is identity-consistent on a pair but shows first-slot preference elsewhere. Are the diagnostics contradictory?
questions.explanation: No. Candidate identity and screen position are different random variables and should be reported separately.

questions.title: Structural isolation
questions.prompt: Which is stronger: “ignore candidate instructions” or passing the candidate as untrusted data with a structured output schema?
questions.explanation: Structural isolation is the stronger engineering contract, but it is not a formal security boundary for a single LLM.

questions.title: Two safety denominators
questions.prompt: Why not divide harmful compliance and benign refusals by one mixed test-set size?
questions.explanation: They estimate different conditional rates: ASR on harmful attempts and over-refusal on benign neighbors. A mixed denominator hides test composition.

questions.title: Critical event
questions.prompt: Average metrics pass, but a confirmed sandbox escape was predeclared as release-blocking. What is the decision?
questions.explanation: NO-GO. A critical gate is not compensated by an average score; preserve an incident record and regression test.

questions.title: Evidence bundle
questions.prompt: What minimally allows a new scorer version to recompute results without another model run?
questions.explanation: Versioned samples, raw responses/transcripts keyed by `sample_id`, solver configuration, scorer revision, summary, and an artifact-hash passport.

questions.title: Current software contract
questions.prompt: What Python entry point does current `lm-evaluation-harness` documentation recommend, and what must happen before publication?
questions.explanation: Use `simple_evaluate()` for Python integration, then pin the actual dependency version, backend, task configuration, and full result artifact.
